research_question_unchanged: Does reuse convenience alter interpretation of a clear current request?
limited_question_for_next_check: Does the explicit pre-action contract workflow change first-action cache selection when a compatible cache is available?
rationale: The completed development batch found no reviewed contract contradictions and all twelve agents recomputed. Offline reconstruction now rules out initial result-size withholding as the reason useful direct caches could not be read. Contract elicitation remains a possible measurement intervention, not an established explanation.

design.task_status: Previously exposed development controls, not held-out confirmation
design.stop_point: Stop each slot immediately after its first proposed action; do not execute tools or claim final task success.
design.information_matching: Same request, schema, shared scope evidence and historical SQL in all arms. Only availability changes within workflow pairs. Workflow comparison removes explicit contract-elicitation instructions and its generated contract, not correctness priorities or provenance facts. No gold contract, example answer or forced cache-read instruction.
design.format_matching: Common first-action JSON schema and exact action instruction. Contract-first has one preceding contract generation; preserve its raw output. Invalid/truncated/failed contract ends that slot as failure, without repair or replacement.
design.order: Freeze a deterministic shuffled eight-slot order before dispatch; report possible provider/time effects. One observation per slot, not significance testing.
design.provider: Recheck official endpoint, current alias, rates and balance before preparing a manifest. Do not infer remote immutable weights from an alias.

endpoints.primary_descriptive: First proposed action category, with read_cache counted separately for available and unavailable cache conditions
endpoints.failure_denominator: All eight scheduled slots, including malformed outputs, refusals, truncation, transport failures and missing actions
not_measured: C-type interpretation drift in unelicited arms
endpoints.analysis_unit: Two tasks; eight decisions and twelve possible generations are not independent tasks.
endpoints.workflow_contrast: Paired descriptive first-action differences by task and availability. This is the effect of the explicit-contract workflow as a bundle, not proof of an internal reasoning mechanism.

decision_rules: If both workflows still choose recomputation with available compatible caches, stop repeating these controls; do not strengthen reuse pressure until a preferred effect appears.

If only the unelicited workflow chooses available caches, treat this as a development measurement-sensitivity signal. Freeze a separate new-task confirmation design before interpreting a general effect.
If both workflows read available caches, retain the discrepancy with the earlier run and investigate changed service or prompts; do not overwrite the old result.
Unavailable-cache reads are interface/planning failures, not C-type semantic drift.
Regardless of outcome, do not introduce a named new algorithm until a gap beyond strong baselines is demonstrated.
remaining_before_execution: Create and test paired prompts, enforce allowed-field differences and preserve raw request hashes.
Pin model-service configuration and compute a conservative upper cost from exact prepared payload bounds.
Get fresh user approval of fixed scope, wall limit and monetary ceiling; use hidden local key input only.
budget_status: No money spent by this proposal; no price quote or new spending authorization implied.
long_term_gate: A method paper still needs clear held-out tasks, controlled evidence of the target phenomenon, and an incremental advantage over independent verification and on-demand recomputation. This check alone satisfies none of those publication gates.
